title: colormap
summary: Set or query a plotting colormap.
description: `colormap` sets or queries the color palette for the current or explicitly targeted plotting context. Public custom maps accept m-by-3 single or double RGB values in [0,1], or uint8 RGB values in [0,255]. Query output is a normalized host double matrix.
behaviors: Named colormaps are also available as RGB array generator functions, so MATLAB forms such as `colormap(jet)`, `colormap(gray(64))`, and `c = turbo(128)` are supported.
`cmap = colormap()` and `cmap = colormap(target)` return an m-by-3 normalized host double matrix. Setter forms do not expose an output.
Public RGB maps are m-by-3 single or double arrays in [0,1], or uint8 arrays in [0,255]. uint8 channels are normalized by division by 255 at the host graphics-state boundary.
The other seven integer classes are a RunMat extension. They are accepted only when every native integer channel is exactly 0 or 1, and strict compatibility mode rejects the form before conversion.
Resident RGB maps are rejected without provider access; colormap metadata and query results are host-resident.
Unknown colormap names raise errors rather than silently falling back.
Colormap state composes naturally with `colorbar`, `imagesc`, `surf`, and filled contour plots.
Untargeted changes apply to the current axes. Targeted axes and figure forms update only the selected plotting context.

faqs.question: What colormaps are available?
faqs.answer: RunMat ships with: `parula`, `colorcube`, `viridis`, `plasma`, `inferno`, `magma`, `turbo`, `jet`, `hot`, `cool`, `spring`, `summer`, `autumn`, `winter`, `gray`, `bone`, `copper`, `pink`, and `lines`. Unknown names raise an error — no silent fallback.

faqs.question: Which colormaps are perceptually uniform?
faqs.answer: `viridis`, `plasma`, `inferno`, and `magma` are designed so that equal steps in data value produce equal perceptual changes in color. Use these for quantitative data where you want the visual contrast to faithfully represent magnitude differences. `parula` is also a good default. Avoid `jet` for quantitative work — it introduces false banding.

faqs.question: Can I define a custom colormap?
faqs.answer: Yes. Pass an m-by-3 single or double matrix in [0,1], or a uint8 matrix in [0,255]. RunMat mode also admits other integer classes when every channel is exactly 0 or 1.
